findings.claim: The new gate's aggregate verdict is derived from the violations strings, not from the per-template pass flags, and no test pins it: gate.pass = (violations.length === 0) where violations = gated.filter(r => !r.pass).flatMap(r => r.violations...). A Gate agent returning {pass: false, violations: []} for a template (GATE_SCHEMA requires the violations array but allows it empty) contributes zero strings, so the workflow returns gate.pass = true and the commit is not blocked although a template failed. The script also never re-checks the agent's pass against save_button_count === 1 / unstyled_input_types empty, so {pass: true, save_button_count: 2} passes as well. No test (the repo has no workflow-JS harness) exercises this aggregation.
findings.fix: Derive the verdict from the flags: `const failed = gated.filter(r => !r.pass || r.save_button_count !== 1 || (r.unstyled_input_types || []).length)`; `gate.pass = failed.length === 0`, with violations falling back to `${r.template}: failed without a stated violation` when r.violations is empty.
findings.evidence: Re-read `git show 1f725ce:skills/feature/fimplement/workflows/config-ui-fidelity-gate.js` in full: L37-48 GATE_SCHEMA requires violations as an array with no minItems; L62-85 the Gate stage returns the agent result unmodified; L88-95 only null results are replaced; L96 flattens r.violations of failed rows; L99 sets gate.pass from violations.length alone. Input {template:'t.html', pass:false, save_button_count:1, violations:[]} -> violations=[] -> gate.pass=true. Exposure set to eventually because the known ledger records that no skill invokes this workflow today (correctness-MAJ-39-r1); this claim is the distinct aggregation defect, not the unreachability. `git ls-files` shows no *.test.js or workflow test harness, so no test pins the aggregation.
